name: Bajaj Finance

headline.text: Trailing twelve months: revenue ₹90,331 cr, NII ₹59,050 cr, PAT ₹22,066 cr.

claims.text: Revenue compounded at 25.2% a year over FY21–FY26 (₹26,673 cr → ₹81,985 cr).

citations.section: Revenue FY26 not located on a page

claims.text: FY26 revenue growth of 19.1% was within its 5-year range (18.6% to 32.7%).

citations.section: Revenue FY26 not located on a page

claims.text: PAT compounded at 34.3% a year over FY21–FY26, ahead of revenue.

citations.excerpt: • Profit after tax (PAT) increased by 15% to C 19,332 crore.

claims.text: Borrowings are a lender's raw material, so debt-to-equity is not a risk signal here; asset quality (NPAs) matters more.
For lenders, loan growth runs through operating cash flow, so CFO-to-profit conversion is not meaningful.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: Overall, I would just say that the first half principally demonstrates the strength and scalability of our business model at this scale to grow 26% is I would say, good growth to be in while maintaining credit costs that, as I've said, that probably it's likely that in the 4 years, this is likely to be one of the lowest years on credit costs.

statements.speaker: Kunal Shah
statements.quote: Hi, so the first question is on growth guidance.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: I would say probably between 26%, 27% growth we should deliver now on a full year basis.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: I think that's just medium term, we maintain a guidance of 20% to 25% on a year lower here and a year higher there.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: In general, our guidance of 16% to 18%.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: So, we remain comfortable in the longer term, we should be able to sustain a 15% to 18% fee income growth is what I would just say to you, Viral.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: We are clear about the medium-term guidance on fees and margins.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: I'm not changing, I must say to you, the longer-term growth guidance of 23% to 25%.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: We've been pruning back, as I said earlier, that we've taken a proactive call that CPL will drop from where it is today at 7% in terms of origination to half business in some business, zero where I have no margin will be zero is the decision management has made and we are going about it.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: I am targeting that next year we should be delivering INR100,000 crores volume between customer centricity, AI and tech transformation and digital transformation, all these three as they come together, that's really what we are aiming to do so that from a push business, we rapidly transition towards being a full business.

statements.speaker: Abhijit Tibrewal
statements.quote: So don't you think this 22% to 24% corridor that we have given for AUM growth can maybe see some upside.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: If you look at quarter 1, logically, but I would wait for second quarter, whether it's top line, which is AUM or PBT growth or ROA or ROE, it does seem we are much better than the guidance that we gave in March.

statements.speaker: Kunal Shah
statements.quote: We guided for margin moderation in FY '27, but are we more comfortable with where the margins stay because you mentioned like cost of borrowing should be range bound.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: Whatever Sandeep has guided for or what we've said, I think that moderation 10 - 15 basis points is what we foresee at this juncture, give us a quarter.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: We expect that it should come back to double-digit growth or the company growth momentum between Q2 and Q3 of FY'27.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: In terms of AUM, we're confident of a 20% to 24% AUM growth, aided by new businesses that we've launched in the last few years as they begin to scale.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: We continue to guide for 4.4% to 4.6%.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: Return on equity came in at 20% in the current quarter, we continue to guide for 19% to 20%.

statements.speaker: Abhishek Murarka
statements.quote: And against that, you're guiding for 145 to 160 bps next year, full year.

statements.speaker: Shreya Shivani
statements.quote: My question is on the long-term guidance of ROA probably inching towards 4.3 - 4.7 percentage.

statements.speaker: Rajeev Jain
statements.quote: ROE guidance of 20 to 22 last 6 years, adjusted for COVID speaks for themselves and during this period, as you can see from a balance sheet standpoint, the balance sheet moved from INR115,000 crores to now INR510,000 crores.

statements.speaker: Sandeep Jain
statements.quote: And just to help you with the math on 4.6%, the guidance metric for the next year on ROA.

statements.speaker: Sandeep Jain
statements.quote: And the guidance that we are giving for next year is 4.4% to 4.6%.

statements.speaker: Sandeep Jain
statements.quote: We have to ensure that we grow nicely, which is where the 22% to 24% guidance has been given.

statements.speaker: Kunal Shah
statements.quote: So on the growth guidance, 22% to 24% apart from SME, which is almost bottomed out, we have started to see the sequential growth and we will get into double digits.

statements.speaker: Sandeep Jain
statements.quote: As regard the profit growth for the next year, 22% to 24% growth in AUM should lead to a little better growth in profitability because if we are supposed to deliver operating efficiency growth of 25% to 40% that Rajeev has talked about, if we see improvement in -- basis points.

management.excerpt: So, I won’t cover Panel 13 and 14, just the only point I'll cover on Panel 13 - 14 is that we’ve launched our first customer risk model from a risk management standpoint, we'll book 500,000 accounts in our B2B business, look at its 3MOB performance. and based on that, start to evaluate that for other lines of businesses.
management.speaker: Rajeev Jain

management.excerpt: So, overall pretty secular growth across all lines of business, in a way, if I look at the gross loan growth because capital book is dialing down, you should add another INR1,000-odd crores that's virtually INR39,000 crores of book growth that we are principally talking about. These are fascinating numbers even for me, I would say.
